findings.title: A 9-16 byte area with a writing probe gets two .param return values, which ptxas and nvPTXCompiler refuse
findings.effect: The PTX is invalid. PTX ISA 7.1.1 says: "For targets sm_20 or higher, PTX restricts functions to a single return value." The .func release notes repeat it: "PTX ISA versions 2.0 and later with target sm_20 or higher support at most one return value." /usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas and libnvptxcompiler_static.a both contain the error string "Multiple return parameters require .register state space", and these return parameters are .param. I did not assemble it, because this review was not allowed to run the board's GPU tools. When the compile fails, load substitution loads the original image, so the whole module runs with no probes. The memory form would have worked, and the plan never falls back to it. Reader-only functions are fine (several input .params are allowed). Only writing probes with words = 2 break, and the entry probe usually writes. Possible fix: return one `.param .align 8 .b8 X_r[16]` array, or take the by-value form only when words == 1.
findings.reachable_today: No, not with the dumped tools. Every by-value dump has __bpftime_tv[8] (lat_mmvq, carry1). carry has a 16-byte area (__bpftime_tl[16] in dumpTV-carry_test) and its entry writes with st.u32 at [%rd14], [%rd14+4], [%rd19], [%rd19+4], which is eligible. It falls back only because its keys are stored by one `st.local.v2.u32 [%rd1+432], {%r2, %r1}`, so they are not forwarded. The same program with its key stores kept separate, or any tool with a 16-byte value or two 8-byte thread-local maps, reaches it from ordinary llvmbpf output.

findings.title: A map fd with a leading zero, or a mov inside a comment, is misread by constant_fd; by value then gives a thread-local helper call area 0
findings.effect: plan_by_value reads fd 10 (or 7). That fd is not in `maps`, so the call is treated as "another map type" (lines 914-917) and the kernel goes by value. route_function_body then gives param4 = 0 (line 1211). At run time the trampoline sees map_info[8] (or [4]) as type 1530, and thread_local_offset returns NULL because area == 0. Every lookup misses and nothing reaches the area, with no fallback. The memory form passes %bpftime_tl_in to every call it does not recognize, so the same misread was harmless there. By value turns it into wrong behaviour.
findings.reachable_today: No. In the dumps every map-fd mov is a plain decimal (`mov.u64 %rdN, 4;`, 14, 194, ...). grep finds no literal with a leading zero and no /* */ comments, and NVPTX writes only // comments, never instruction-like text.

findings.title: A block-comment copy of a labelled access (or ret) makes the per-line count match, so the real access is not rewritten
findings.effect: pieces() strips the label, so it records the real access once (access_lines = 1). line_statement() strips comments one line at a time and cannot see that it is inside /* */, so it counts the commented line instead (on_lines = 1). The two maps are equal, so the plan is accepted (lines 1010-1027). by_value_rewrite replaces only the commented line, and done == want. The real `ld.u32 %rd17, [%rd15]` stays, and %rd15 is now `mov.u64 %rd15, 1`, so this is a generic load from address 1: a misaligned or illegal address, and the kernel faults. In the ret variant, rets (2) equals ret_lines (2), but the labelled real ret returns without st.param of the return words. The kernel then stores an undefined value into __bpftime_tv.
findings.reachable_today: No. grep -c '/\*' is 0 in dumpN70-lat_mmvq, dumpTV-carry_test and dumpTV-carry1_test. NVPTX and llvmbpf emit no block comments and put labels on their own lines.

findings.title: constant_key trusts a def count that misses redux.sync and stacksave writes, so a register they overwrite is taken for its mov constant
findings.effect: build_index (line 294) skips every op whose name starts with "st" or "red", so redux.sync and stacksave are not counted as defs of %r1. count_defs is 1 and the recorded def is `mov.u32 %r1, 0`. forwarded_key returns %r1, because the redux comes before the store. constant_key then gives key 0, and the plan maps the value to entry 0's halves. The runtime key is the warp sum, which may be another entry or out of range (NULL in the memory form). The memory form forwards the register itself (`mov.u32 %bptl_k0, %r1`), so it is right. By value reads and writes the wrong entry's bytes.
findings.reachable_today: No. grep -c 'redux|stacksave' is 0 in the dumps, and eBPF has no operation that lowers to them.

findings.title: Storing a lookup result into its own value passes the allowlist and stores 1 instead of the address bits
findings.effect: st32 matches with the address equal to hit and `other` equal to the same hit. The "two lookup results" check only fires for two different registers, and %rd9 is 64-bit. The access becomes `cvt.u32.u64 %bptv_h0, %rd9`, but %rd9 is now the constant 1. The value stores 1 where the memory form stored the low 32 bits of the area's generic address, which changes what a program that keeps a pointer in a map value reads back.
findings.reachable_today: No. In the dumps a lookup result appears only as an address or in a compare with 0. A store of the pointer itself needs a program that leaks a map-value pointer into a map.

findings.title: A guard on the line before a ret moves onto the give-back, so the ret runs unconditionally
findings.reachable_today: no. LLVM's NVPTX printer puts a guard and its instruction on one line; every ret in the dumps (dumpTV-lat_mmvq, dumpTV-carry1_test) is "\tret;" or "\t@%bpftime_off ret;". This needs hand-written or edited PTX.

findings.title: Line-based access and ret counts can be satisfied by comment or .loc lines, leaving a real access or ret unrewritten
findings.effect:
(a) by_value_rewrite (line 1055) replaces the commented line, which stays inside the comment, so done == want. The real "st.u32 [%rd9], %rd14" stays a memory store through %rd9, which is now "mov.u64 %rd9, 1". That is a generic store to address 1: a misaligned or illegal address fault, and the kernel launch fails. The area is not updated either.
(b) The give-back goes before the glued ret only. The "$L__BB0_4: ret;" path returns without writing F_bpftime_tv_r0, and the kernel's st.local stores an undefined value into the area.
findings.reachable_today: no. llvmbpf emits neither block comments nor .loc (no debug info), and it never puts a label on the same line as ret. Both need PTX that the pass pipeline does not produce today.

findings.title: By-value call site repeats any text before the call's '@' in each write-back line, and puts the write-back after the rest of the line
findings.input:
The kernel call line holds other statements, and the probe function writes the area.
(a) Kernel inline asm on one line, "{.reg .pred p; setp.ne.u32 p, %0, 0; @p add.s32 %1, %1, 1; @p exit;}". After kretprobe it becomes:
{.reg .pred p; setp.ne.u32 p, %r20, 0; @p add.s32 %r5, %r5, 1; @p call __retprobe_func__K;
head.find('@') (line 1352) finds the add's guard, so predicate = "@p add.s32 %r5, %r5, 1; @p ".
(b) Stub path with a trailing statement: "call __probe_func__K; @%p3 bra $L__BB0_4;".
findings.reachable_today: no. The kprobe entry pass puts the call on its own line. The kretprobe pass ends the call with "\n", and LLVM/nvcc emit one statement per line. Only multi-statement inline asm (a), or the unused __bpftime_cuda__kernel_trace stub path (b), produces these lines. The dumps' call sites (dumpTV-lat_mmvq, dumpTV-carry1_test, including "@p call __retprobe_func__pt_kdiv") are all on lines of their own.

findings.title: Load-bearing fail-closed checks in plan_by_value have no test; the fallback table never asserts the reason
findings.input:
Checks with no test, at nv_thread_local_routing.cpp lines:
(1) 935-936, lookup result written twice. Two thread-local lookups on two branches joined into one register (map 4, max_entries 2):
  @%p0 bra $L1; mov.u32 %r1, 0; st.local.u32 [%rd4+508], %r1; ... {callseq 9 ... _bpf_helper_ext_0001 ... ld.param.b64 %rd9, [retval0+0];} bra.uni $L2;
  $L1: mov.u32 %r2, 1; st.local.u32 [%rd4+508], %r2; ... {callseq 10 ... _bpf_helper_ext_0001 ... ld.param.b64 %rd9, [retval0+0];}
  $L2: st.u32 [%rd9], %rd14;
Also `ld.u32 %rd9, [%rd9]; st.u32 [%rd9], %rd14;`. This line is the only guard: the use loop accepts any `ld.param.b64 %rd9, [retval0+0]` as 'the definition' (972).
(2) 921-924, another call-block shape. A thread-local lookup callseq holding an extra instruction, e.g. `add.s64 %rd30, %rd31, 1;`. The by-value branch (1157-1168) replaces the whole block with `mov.u64 %rd9, 1`, so the extra instruction would be dropped.
(3) 1026, only one direction tested. Only rets > ret_lines is tested (labelled ret); ret_lines > rets (e.g. a ret glued to `.loc`) is not.
(4) 998-1001, `byte % 4` (a descriptor offset not 4-aligned).
Untested but redundant: 899 (unterminated block: the memory form throws), 918 for helper 3 (delete of a thread-local map returns -1 without reading the area), 957 (exit ends the thread), 965 (falls through to 'other use' anyway), 1328-1333 'no definition' (the memory form throws later), and the defensive fails at 1069 and 1161.
The 'Any other form' table checks only `byvalue_fallbacks.size()==1` (388), never `why`.
No test covers: two kernels in one module (one by value, one falling back), a probe function that both reads and writes (call with rets and a predicated store-back), several call sites of one probe in a kernel, or the accepted `setp.eq.s64 %p, 0, %rd9` form (cmp0r).
findings.effect: If (1) or (2) is weakened, by-value silently rewrites programs that must keep the area in memory, and no unit test fails. Example for (1): pointers[%rd9] is overwritten by the second lookup, so the store always lands in key 1's half (%bptv_h2) even on the key-0 path. For (2), the block's extra instruction is lost. A table row can also pass because a different check fired than the one its label names.
findings.reachable_today: The shape in (1) is yes: llvmbpf joins lookups from several branches into one register (route_function_body's sum_defs handles exactly this; carry1's %rd54 is written by two sum-map lookups). The checks themselves work today; only the tests are missing.

findings.title: A store of the lookup pointer itself passes the plan and stores 1 instead of the address
findings.effect: Memory form: stores the low 32 bits of the value's generic local address. By value: the lookup becomes `mov.u64 %rd9, 1` and the store becomes `cvt.u32.u64 %bptv_h0, %rd9`, so 1 is stored and the exit reads 1. The program's meaning changes. This also contradicts the header claim (nv_thread_local_routing.hpp:62-63) that the area's address never leaves the rewritten accesses. Fix: refuse when the stored register is the pointer.
findings.reachable_today: No current tool does this. It is plausible from eBPF `*(u32 *)v = (u32)(long)v`, since NVPTX emits truncating stores with the 64-bit register (lat's `st.u32 [%rd9], %rd14`).

findings.title: Line-based ret/access matching can cancel against the tokenizer's counts (.loc glue, block comments)
findings.effect:
A: by_value_rewrite (1062) puts the give-back only before the .loc ret. The labelled ret returns without st.param of <fn>_bpftime_tv_r0, and the kernel stores that unwritten return parameter into __bpftime_tv, so an undefined value replaces the area.
B: the commented line is 'rewritten' and the real `st.u32 [%rd9], %rd14` stays, with %rd9 = 1. That is a generic store to address 1: a misaligned/illegal address kernel fault.
Third case: the comment body becomes live PTX (ptxas error, or live code).
findings.reachable_today: No. The lat_mmvq, carry and carry1 dumps contain 0 .loc/.file directives and 0 block comments.

findings.title: Header top paragraph and trampoline comment are stale; the commit and header overstate what is checked
findings.input:
Stale text, now contradicted:
- hpp 3-11: 'every probed kernel gets a kernel-scope .local area ... passed to each of its probe functions as their one parameter ... every other map helper call (1, 2, 3) gets the address'.
- default_trampoline.cu 244-248: 'a kernel-scope .local the agent's routing adds to every probed kernel'.
A lat kernel now has no __bpftime_tl, helpers 1-3 get 0, and a kernel whose probes do not reach the area has none.
Overstated checks:
- Commit message: 'every map helper call must name its map with a constant'. Only helpers 1-3 are checked (cpp 909-910), so a `_bpf_helper_ext_0025` call with a register map fd passes.
- hpp 47-48: compares with 0 must be 'on lines of their own'. Only accesses and rets are line-checked, so `$L: setp.eq.s64 %p1, %rd9, 0;` passes.
findings.effect:
Readers of the header and trampoline are told every probed kernel carries the address-form area and that helpers get its address, which no longer holds. The two overstatements are harmless today: helpers other than 1-3 never get the area, and a compare is not rewritten.
Checked and accurate:
- PTX ISA 5.1.5, 5.1.6.4, 7.1, 9.4.1 (zero-extension for non-signed types; signed loads fall back) and 6.5.1. mov.b64 pack/unpack exists since PTX 1.0, and h0 is the low word.
- 0.0210/0.0238 ns and 54.33->55.88 t/s (v1).
- tvpass equals the pass output byte for byte.
- The fallback dumps (carry, hist, latold, tlatomic) are byte-identical to n70.
- 3,880,960 thread executions; tlatomic's area is __bpftime_tl[24].
- The halves' order is never observed, because 64-bit accesses fall back for the whole kernel.
- The changed sum-map expectation is safe: the trampoline reads helper 1/2's last argument only for 1530, and nothing else in nv_attach_impl references __bpftime_tl.
findings.reachable_today: Yes, but documentation only: no PTX is affected.

findings.title: Pre-existing: constant_fd reads PTX octal map fds as decimal, so by value can replace the wrong map's lookup
findings.effect: constant_fd returns 10. plan_by_value then treats this as a lookup of thread-local map 10: it becomes `mov.u64 %rd9, 1` and the load reads %bptv_h of map 10 instead of map 8's value. The memory form had the same misrouting (it routed to map 10's area), so this predates 1d95c160, but it now also reaches the by-value rewrite. Contrast constant_key, which is strict decimal.
findings.reachable_today: No. LLVM prints decimal immediates without leading zeros.

verdicts.reason: The trace on the real lat_mmvq probe shape, with one inserted instruction, reproduces the claim. build_index (nv_thread_local_routing.cpp:294) skips any statement whose mnemonic starts with "red" or "st". That covers redux.sync and stacksave, and both write a destination register. So count_defs("%r4") is 1, and the recorded def is `mov.u32 %r4, 0`. forwarded_key returns %r4 because the redux comes before the store. constant_key (line 847) returns key 0, and plan_by_value (lines 929-937) maps the lookup result to entry 0. route_function_body (lines 1157-1168) then replaces the call with `mov.u64 %rd15, 1`, and the loads become cvt moves from %bptv_h0/%bptv_h1. At run time %r4 holds the warp sum. In the memory form the key is that sum (key_into: `mov.u32 %bptl_k0, %r4`), and `setp.lt.u32 ..., 1` / selp gives NULL whenever the sum is 1 or more. By value always gives a non-null pointer to entry 0, so the program reads and writes bytes the memory form never reaches. The input is valid PTX: the module is `.version 8.1` / `.target sm_87`, while redux.sync needs sm_80 / PTX 7.0 and stacksave needs PTX 7.3. It is not reachable today: the dumps contain no redux, stacksave or stackrestore, eBPF has nothing that lowers to them, and LLVM's NVPTX output does not write a virtual register twice like this. Severity low (fail-open on a hypothetical input).

I traced the code on the finding's input. A 16-byte area whose probe writes gets two `.param .b64` return values, both on the function and on the call. Nothing in `plan_by_value` or the kernel step limits a writer to one word, and nothing falls back to the memory form. I did not assemble the result. I inferred the refusal from two sources: the PTX ISA text on disk says sm_20+ functions return a single value, and the exact error strings are in both ptxas and libnvptxcompiler_static.a. No 16-byte by-value module was ever compiled. Every by-value PTX under bpftime-gpu-work has `__bpftime_tv[8]`, and the commit message says only lat and carry1, both 8-byte areas, ran by value. So the current dumps do not reach this case, but ordinary llvmbpf output can.
verdicts.evidence:
The code trace (/home/jetson/src/bpftime-proto-70f7/attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_thread_local_routing.cpp):
- L876: `plan_by_value` refuses only when `area_bytes > BYVALUE_MAX_BYTES` (16).
- L1253 rounds the area to 8-byte words; L1269 sets `const uint64_t words = area_bytes / 8;`, so words = 2.
- The access rule allows a write anywhere in the value: `off % 4 != 0 || off + 4 > value_size[hit] || byte % 4 != 0` rejects, otherwise `(load ? pl.reads : pl.writes) = true;`. In the finding's first variant (one 16-byte value), stores at +8 and +12 pass. The test's variant (map 4 at offset 8) passes too.
- No other check looks at `words` or `writes`. The kernel step (around L1325) uses by-value whenever every called plan is `ok`.
- L1374-1386, the call site, emits `call (%bpftime_tv_r0, %bpftime_tv_r1), __probe_func__kern, (%bpftime_tv_a0, %bpftime_tv_a1);`.
- L1491-1498 build `ret_list` with one `.param .b64 <f>_bpftime_tv_r<w>` per word, and L1536-1538 insert it as `(ret_list) name(...)`.
- `tv_give_back` (L1034) writes `st.param.b64` to each `_r<w>` before every ret.

The committed test confirms the output text. test_thread_local_byvalue.cpp:233-260, "The second word of a 16-byte area is two more halves", requires exactly `.visible .func (.param .b64 __probe_func__kern_bpftime_tv_r0, .param .b64 __probe_func__kern_bpftime_tv_r1) __probe_func__kern(` and the two-return call. The test only compares text.

Why the PTX is refused (from reading only; I did not run ptxas):
- The PTX ISA text on disk, /home/jetson/src/bpftime-gpu-work/step0b/c5-guarantees/docs/text/ptx-isa.txt, says at line 7083: "For targets sm_20 or higher, PTX restricts functions to a single return value, and a .param byte array should be used to return objects that do not fit into a register". At line 48183: "PTX ISA versions 2.0 and later with target sm_20 or higher support at most one return value." The dumps use `.version 8.1` / `.target sm_87`.
- `strings /usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas` and `strings /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libnvptxcompiler_static.a` both contain "Multiple return parameters require .register state space" and "Function with multiple return values is not allowed with ABI". Here the return parameters are `.param`.
- No PTX under bpftime-gpu-work has a `.func` with two `.param` return entries.

What happens when the compile fails:
- `cuLibraryLoadData`'s hook (nv_attach_impl_frida_setup.cpp:1128-1148) loads the original image when the patched one fails, as CLAUDE.md's load-substitution section says. The whole fatbin then runs unprobed.
- The pass has no retry in the memory form: nv_attach_impl.cpp only logs the by-value stats at 1059-1063.

Reachability:
- `grep -rho '__bpftime_tv\[[0-9]*\]'` over all .ptx in bpftime-gpu-work finds only `__bpftime_tv[8]`, 7 times.
- dumpTV-carry_test has `__bpftime_tl[16]` and 4 `st.local.v2.u32` lines. That vector key store is why carry falls back, as the commit message also says ("carry stores its keys with one vector store, so they are not forwarded").
- So carry with scalar key stores, any 16-byte value, or two 8-byte thread-local maps with a writing probe would hit this. The entry probe usually writes.

verdicts.reason: I traced the exact input through plan_by_value, route_function_body and by_value_rewrite, and the finding holds. The allowlist never checks that the stored value is a register other than the lookup result. The plan is accepted, the lookup becomes `mov.u64 %rd9, 1`, and the store turns into `cvt.u32.u64 %bptv_h0, %rd9`. The area's word therefore gets 1. The old memory form stored the low 32 bits of the value's generic address (cvta.local of the area plus its offset). The rewritten PTX is valid, so ptxas accepts it and the value changes silently. This also contradicts the header's stated premise (nv_thread_local_routing.hpp:61) that the area's address "never leaves the probe functions' rewritten accesses". The matching load case is already refused: `ld.u32 %rd9, [%rd9]` gives %rd9 a second definition, which fails at line 935. Only the store slips through. It is not reachable today: a PCRE search of every dump under proto/target-shape for `st.[ub]32 [%rdN...], %rdN` finds nothing. It needs a program that stores a map-value pointer into that value. A privileged eBPF program can do that, and bpftime has no verifier by default. Severity is low.
verdicts.evidence:
Input (in the real dump's shape: dumpN70-lat_mmvq has `ld.param.b64 %rd14, [retval0+0]; } // callseq 9` followed by `st.u32 [%rd9], %rd14;`, a 64-bit source register):
  { // callseq 9 ... _bpf_helper_ext_0001 ... ld.param.b64 %rd9, [retval0+0]; } // callseq 9

Rewrite:
- route_function_body lines 1157-1166 replace the call block with `mov.u64 %rd9, 1; // bpftime thread-local lookup by value`. The same happens in the real dumpTV output: `mov.u64 %rd9, 1; // ... map 4`.

- tv_give_back (lines 1034-1041) returns {h0,h1} to the kernel, which stores it into __bpftime_tv.

Old memory form: kernel `cvta.local.u64 AREA_REG, AREA_SYM` (lines 1411-1414), and the routed lookup gives `%rd9 = AREA_IN + offset` (selp at line 1200). The st.u32 then stores the low 32 bits of that generic address, a 4-aligned address that is never 1.

Reachability: `grep -P 'st\.[ub]32\s+\[(%rd\d+)[^\]]*\],\s*\1;'` over /home/jetson/src/bpftime-gpu-work/proto/target-shape/*/*.ptx finds no matches, so this only happens with a hypothetical program.

verdicts.reason:
I traced the exact input through the code and the claimed effect happens, but only for a hypothetical input. The comment variant needs nothing but the C++ to show it. count_defs strips comments, so %rd5 has exactly one definition. constant_fd then searches the raw body, comments included, takes the first match (the one in the comment) and reads fd 7. In the octal variant the C++ half is also certain: the "(-?\d+)" capture plus std::stoll, and parse_int's strtoll base 10 for a direct literal, read "010" as 10. That this is wrong at run time (ptxas reads 010 as 8) comes from the PTX ISA literal grammar; I could not run ptxas here, but the comment variant shows the same effect without it.

The effect needs the misread fd to be in neither maps nor sums. If it were a sum map with a device copy, the call would become a sum lookup instead, a different wrong result. The plan (line 912) and the rewrite (line 1131) call constant_fd on the same probe-function text, so both misread the same way and the "by-value lookup not planned" check never fires. In by-value mode the call then gets param4 = 0, and the trampoline returns NULL for a type-1530 map with area 0. Every lookup misses, with no fallback.

Before 1d95c160, every probe function a kernel called was routed (the diff removes the unconditional `routed_functions.insert(n)`). An unrecognised fd then got AREA_IN, so the same misread was harmless. constant_fd itself is older code; the commit leaves it unchanged and only adds the call in plan_by_value.

Not reachable today. Across the dumps, my greps found no map-fd mov with a leading-zero literal, no `[param0+0]` store of one, no `//` comment containing "mov." and no `/*` comment. Severity: low.
